subject: Private deployment: custody & attestation for on-prem addendum
messages:
From: Kendra Miller <kendra.miller@acmehealth.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment questions: custody / proof for on-prem install

Diego —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our procurement team is drafting the order form + MSA addendum for the on-prem deployment. A few items came up we need clarified before we move to redlines:

1) License scope: we need confirmation that the license covers a single customer-managed cluster (we do not want a sublicensable or transfer-right).
2) Key custody: we require an option where Acme holds the encryption keys (customer-managed KMS/HSM). Is that supported and are there any feature gaps?
3) Audit / attestation: our security team asks for a vendor-signed attestation that the delivered binaries match the published artifact hash and that access logs (audit logs) will be retained for X months. We also want a brief description of what evidence Redwood can provide if we request a limited on-site or remote audit.

Can you loop in legal and security so we can get proposed contract language?

-Kendra
Kendra Miller
Director, IT Procurement
Acme Health

From: diego.fernandez@redwood.com <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Kendra Miller <kendra.miller@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-18T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions: custody / proof for on-prem install

Kendra — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (legal) and Rishi (security) to draft suggested addendum language and a short evidence package.

Laura / Rishi: can you review the three asks above and propose:
- Short contract language for the MSA addendum (license scope + key custody clause + audit window)
- A minimal attestation template Acme can rely on (we have an internal "attestation" PDF we use for partner installs)
- A palatable approach for on-site vs remote evidence requests (what we can commit to vs what requires separate SOW)

I attached a rough skeleton addendum (RDW_Private_Addendum_v1.docx) and our attestation template (Attestation_Template.pdf) to start.

Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: RDW_Private_Addendum_v1.docx, Attestation_Template.pdf

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com, Kendra Miller <kendra.miller@acmehealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-18T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions: custody / proof for on-prem install

Kendra / Diego —

Quick take from legal. Below are suggested clause fragments you can propose in the addendum; happy to redline your version into the RDW_Private_Addendum_v1.docx.

1) License scope (sample): "Provider grants Customer a non-transferable, non-sublicensable license to deploy the Redwood Inference runtime, binaries, and associated artifacts on Customer-managed infrastructure exclusively for Customer internal business operations. Provider retains all IP rights; Customer may not distribute or resell the software."

2) Key custody: "Customer may elect to manage cryptographic keys used for data encryption via Customer-managed KMS/HSM. Where Customer elects customer-managed keys, Provider shall not have access to plaintext data and shall not be obligated to provide live-support access that requires decryption without a court order or explicit Customer consent. Provider may provide guidance and tooling for key integration; any additional engineering work to support custom HSMs will be scoped in a separate SOW."

3) Audit / attestation: two-pronged approach we recommend: (a) a vendor attestation for delivered artifacts and logging coverage (we can provide Attestation_Template.pdf), and (b) a limited remote evidence package (secure Drive folder with artifact hashes, log retention policy, sample redacted logs) within 10 business days of request. On-site, physical audits or deep forensic inspections require prior notice and a signed SOW to cover incremental costs and access coordination.

We suggest including a defined "audit window" (e.g., up to 4 hours of remote analyst time per calendar quarter, additional hours billable) and a scope list (only runtime binaries, configuration manifests, and audit logs; no access to customer plaintext).

I'll prepare a redline and flag anything that would be an SLA exception.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com, Kendra Miller <kendra.miller@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions: custody / proof for on-prem install

Kendra — adding the security checklist details so Acme knows what to expect from the evidence package.

What we can provide out-of-band (no SOW):
- Binary artifact SHA256 hashes and a signed checksum manifest.
- Deployment runbook excerpt describing default control-plane ports, recommended RBAC configuration, and expected log destinations (we included runbook-sample.txt).
- Audit log retention: default 90 days; we can extend in order form for an additional fee. Logs include authentication events, API calls to the serving runtime, and system-level alerts.
- Remote proof: we can provide a time-limited read-only access session to a sanitized log bundle or a recorded session showing hash verification.

What requires SOW / on-site:
- Host-level forensic access (e.g., image capture) or deep forensic review.
- Custom HSM engineering and integration beyond standard KMS APIs (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS).

Operational suggestion: agree on a 10-business-day turnaround for remote evidence requests and include a clause limiting frequency to one full evidence pull per 90 days unless mutually agreed. That keeps operational overhead predictable.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: diego.fernandez@redwood.com <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Kendra Miller <kendra.miller@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-20T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions: custody / proof for on-prem install

Kendra — appreciate the quick review. Attached is a redlined addendum (RDW_Private_Addendum_v1.docx) with Laura's clauses inserted and Rishi's operational limits noted. Also attached: Attestation_Template.pdf and the runbook-sample.txt for your security team's review.

To summarize the proposed commercial points:
- License: single-customer, non-transferable deployment (no sublicensing).
- Keys: customer-managed KMS supported; Redwood will not retain plaintext nor support decryption without explicit customer authorization.
- Evidence: vendor attestation (signed PDF) + remote evidence package available within 10 business days; one full evidence pull per 90 days included, additional requests billable. On-site forensic or extended engagements require SOW.

If Acme is OK with the above, Laura can incorporate final language into the MSA addendum and we'll route the order form for signature (DocuSign link below). If you'd prefer an escrow-style custody (third-party deposit of artifacts), we can add a clause and outline costs — Laura, please flag for pricing if needed.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/ABCDEF123456
Drive folder (evidence & redlines): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-addendum

Thanks — happy to set a 30 minute call to walk security through the runbook.

Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: RDW_Private_Addendum_v1.docx, Attestation_Template.pdf, runbook-sample.txt

From: Kendra Miller <kendra.miller@acmehealth.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, legal@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-20T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions: custody / proof for on-prem install

Diego / team —

Thanks for the thorough response and the attachments. Acme is generally comfortable with the approach. A couple of follow-ups from our side before we finalize the redline:

1) Can you confirm costs for extended log retention to 365 days (we may need this for compliance)?
2) For escrow-style custody: we would like an option where a third-party (neutral escrow) holds a signed artifact snapshot and a sealed key. Please provide estimated costs/lead time and whether Redwood will accept that model as equivalent to the vendor attestation.
3) Please add the proposed "one full evidence pull per 90 days" language into the addendum so we can see the exact wording.

I'll ask our legal to upload a clean MSA + redline if we have anything to counter — otherwise we'll review your docx and get back within two business days.

-Kendra
